newsitem.title: CUBA: Bahamas-based company to launch Cuban investment fund.
newsitem.headline: Bahamas-based company to launch Cuban investment fund.

text.p: A Canadian investment expert said Monday he was launching a Bahamas-based investment fund to provide capital for medium-sized Canadian companies doing business in Cuba.
The move reflects continuing Canadian business interest in the communist-ruled island. The fund will be one of the first aimed at raising capital for investment in Cuba.

Charles Villeneuve told reporters the fund manager would be Ecomatrix S.A., a Bahamas-based company, and would aim to start operating in March. He added he had received commitments for about $C50 million ($37 million) from potential investors.
The fund, called the Cuba Growth Fund Ltd., would start operating with about $C100 million ($74.6 million) but could grow to about $500 million ($73 million), he added.

Villeneuve said the fund would predominantly invest in listed Canadian companies with substantial business on the island. He added the aim was not large companies -- which are more easily able to raise funds themselves -- but medium-sized companies seeking to expand.
Canadian firms, mostly in the mining, oil exploration and tourism sectors, have been leading investors in Cuba since the island began a drive to attract foreign capital in the early 1990s.
Villeneuve said the fund would aim to have interests in about 15 to 20 firms, focusing on sectors such as tourism, restaurants, real estate and construction.

The Cuba Growth Fund follows the launch last year of an investment fund by Havana Asset Management, a Bahamas-based group which has a representative office in Cuba. HAM manages a fund known as Beta Gran Caribe Limited which raised money in February 1996 for investment in businesses with interests in Cuba.
